source.text: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אָמ֑וֹץ עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The word which saw Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

en.L: The word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
en.B: This is the word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
en.R: This is the message that Isaiah son of Amoz received from God in a vision. It was about Judah and Jerusalem.

es.L: La palabra que vio Isaías hijo de Amoz acerca de Judá y Jerusalén.
es.B: Esta es la palabra que Isaías hijo de Amoz vio acerca de Judá y de Jerusalén.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que Isaías hijo de Amoz recibió de Dios en una visión. Trataba sobre Judá y Jerusalén.

sw.L: Neno ambalo Isaya mwana wa Amozi aliliona kuhusu Yuda na Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Hili ndilo neno ambalo Isaya mwana wa Amozi aliliona kuhusu Yuda na Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao Isaya mwana wa Amozi aliupokea kutoka kwa Mungu katika maono. Ulihusu Yuda na Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: the word that he saw: a message received by revelation
decisions.reason: A word is something heard, yet Isaiah "saw" it. The verb is the one behind "vision" in 1:1: the prophet perceived God's message as a seer does (Amos 1:1; Micah 1:1).

decisions.choice: a new title: it introduces the messages that follow
decisions.reason: After the title of the whole book in 1:1, this second title opens a new collection of messages about Judah and Jerusalem. It most likely covers chapters 2-4, which begin and end with a picture of Zion restored (2:2-4; 4:2-6).

decisions.choice: received from God in a vision
decisions.reason: Readable explains "saw": God gave Isaiah the message in a vision.

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים נָכ֨וֹן יִֽהְיֶ֜ה הַ֤ר בֵּית־יְהוָה֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הֶהָרִ֔ים וְנִשָּׂ֖א מִגְּבָע֑וֹת וְנָהֲר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be at [the] end of the days, established will be [the] mountain of [the] house of Yahweh at [the] head of the mountains, and lifted up above [the] hills, and will stream to it all the nations.

en.L: And it will be at the end of the days [that] the mountain of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be established at the head of the mountains, \q and [will be] lifted up above the hills, \q and all the nations will stream to it.
en.B: In days to come, the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house will stand firm, the chief of all the mountains, \q rising high above the hills, \q and the nations will all stream toward it.
en.R: In the future, the mountain where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple stands will become the greatest mountain of all. \q It will rise higher than any hill. \q People from every nation will come to it like a river flowing in.

es.L: Y sucederá al final de los días [que] el monte de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} quedará firme a la cabeza de los montes, \q y [será] elevado por encima de las colinas, \q y fluirán hacia él todas las naciones.
es.B: En los días venideros, el monte de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estará firme, el principal de todos los montes, \q alzándose por encima de las colinas, \q y todas las naciones acudirán a él como un río.
es.R: En el futuro, el monte donde está el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} llegará a ser el monte más importante de todos. \q Se alzará más alto que cualquier colina. \q Gente de todas las naciones llegará a él como un río que corre.

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku za mwisho, [kwamba] mlima wa nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} utaimarishwa juu ya vilele vya milima, \q na [utainuliwa] juu kuliko vilima, \q na mataifa yote yatamiminika kwake.
sw.B: Katika siku zijazo, mlima wa nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} utasimama imara, mkuu kuliko milima yote, \q ukiinuka juu kuliko vilima, \q nayo mataifa yote yatatiririka kuuelekea.
sw.R: Siku zijazo, mlima ambapo hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} limesimama utakuwa mlima mkuu kuliko yote. \q Utakuwa juu kuliko kilima chochote. \q Watu wa kila taifa watakuja kwake kama mto unaotiririka.

decisions.choice: at the end of the days: in the time to come, the future God has in view
decisions.reason: The phrase points beyond the present to a coming time when God's purpose is fulfilled (Genesis 49:1; Numbers 24:14; Deuteronomy 4:30). It does not by itself mean the end of the world. The New Testament speaks of "the last days" as having begun (Acts 2:17; Hebrews 1:2).

decisions.choice: Micah 4:1-3 has the same prophecy
decisions.reason: Verses 2-4 appear almost word for word in Micah 4:1-3, where Micah adds the picture of each person sitting under his own vine and fig tree (Micah 4:4). Isaiah and Micah prophesied in the same years (Micah 1:1). The text does not say whether one prophet took it from the other or both used an older oracle.

decisions.choice: the head of the mountains: Zion raised above every height, and the nations streaming up to it
decisions.reason: Mount Zion is not a tall mountain. The picture is of its honor: the place where God is worshiped will stand above every other height (Psalm 48:2-3). The verb "stream" is used of rivers, so the nations flowing up a mountain is itself a wonder. The same word "lifted up" returns in verses 12-14 for every proud height that God will bring low.

decisions.choice: In days to come (Balanced); In the future (Readable)
decisions.reason: These keep the sense of a coming time without suggesting the end of the world. Literal keeps "at the end of the days".

decisions.choice: where the LORD's temple stands ... like a river flowing in
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the house of the LORD" as the temple and spells out the picture of a stream.

decisions.choice: al final de los días (L); en los días venideros (B); en el futuro (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, B and R speak of a time to come without suggesting the end of the world; L keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: "nyumba ya BWANA" (L, B), "hekalu la BWANA" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Kings and Chronicles for the temple, kept through Isaiah.

source.text: וְֽהָלְכ֞וּ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים וְאָמְרוּ֙ לְכ֣וּ׀וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה אֶל־הַר־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־בֵּית֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹרֵ֨נוּ֙ מִדְּרָכָ֔יו וְנֵלְכָ֖ה בְּאֹרְחֹתָ֑יו כִּ֤י מִצִּיּוֹן֙ תֵּצֵ֣א תוֹרָ֔ה וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה מִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go peoples many and say, come and let us go up to [the] mountain of Yahweh, to [the] house of [the] God of Jacob, and he will teach us from his ways, and we will walk in his paths. For from Zion will go out instruction, and [the] word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.

en.L: And many peoples will go and say, "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the house of the God of Jacob, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will teach us from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and we will walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths." \q For from Zion will go out instruction, \q and the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from Jerusalem.
en.B: Peoples in great numbers will set out, saying, "Come, let us climb to the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, up to the house of Jacob's God, \q so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may show us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways and we may walk on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths." \q For instruction will go out from Zion, \q and the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from Jerusalem.
en.R: Many peoples will come and say, "Let us go up to the mountain of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Let us go to the temple of the God of Israel. \q He will teach us how to live, and we will do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says." \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s teaching will go out from Zion. \q His word will go out from Jerusalem.

es.L: Y muchos pueblos irán y dirán: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, y subamos al monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, a la casa del Dios de Jacob, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos enseñará de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} caminos, y andaremos por {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sendas». \q Porque de Sion saldrá la instrucción, \q y de Jerusalén la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Pueblos numerosos se pondrán en camino, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, subamos al monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, a la casa del Dios de Jacob, \q para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos muestre {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} caminos y andemos por {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sendas». \q Porque de Sion saldrá la instrucción, \q y de Jerusalén la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Muchos pueblos vendrán y dirán: «Subamos al monte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Vamos al templo del Dios de Israel. \q Él nos enseñará cómo vivir, y haremos lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dice». \q La enseñanza {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} saldrá de Sion. \q Su palabra saldrá de Jerusalén.

sw.L: Na watu wengi watakwenda na kusema, "Njooni, na tupande kwenda mlimani mwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwenye nyumba ya Mungu wa Yakobo, \q naye atatufundisha njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, nasi tutatembea katika mapito {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}." \q Kwa maana kutoka Sayuni yatatoka mafundisho, \q na neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kutoka Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Watu wa mataifa mengi watakwenda wakisema, "Njooni, tupande mlimani mwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, hadi nyumbani mwa Mungu wa Yakobo, \q ili atuonyeshe njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, nasi tutembee katika mapito {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}." \q Kwa maana mafundisho yatatoka Sayuni, \q na neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kutoka Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Watu wa mataifa mengi watakuja na kusema, "Twendeni juu mlimani mwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Twendeni hekaluni mwa Mungu wa Israeli. \q Atatufundisha jinsi ya kuishi, nasi tutafanya anayosema." \q Mafundisho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yatatoka Sayuni. \q Neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} litatoka Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: instruction: God's teaching for how to live
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or direction, the guidance a parent or priest gives. It can name the law of Moses, but here it is the instruction the nations come to learn, set beside "the word of Yahweh" (compare 1:10).

decisions.choice: the peoples' words end with "his paths"
alternatives: the peoples' words run to the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. The last line, "for from Zion instruction will go out", is read here as the prophet's own explanation of why the nations come. It may also be the end of what the peoples say.

decisions.choice: let us go up: the pilgrims' words, now on the lips of the nations
decisions.reason: Israel went "up" to the LORD's house for the feasts (Psalm 122:1-4; Psalm 24:3). Now the nations make that journey, and they come to be taught. "Teach us from his ways" means teach us his ways, or some of them.

decisions.choice: the God of Israel ... how to live ... do what he says ... teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "Israel" for "Jacob", the ancestor whose name the people bore, and explains "his ways" and "walk in his paths" as living the way God teaches. "Teaching" renders the word for instruction, as everywhere at this level.

decisions.choice: quotation marks « » for the peoples' words
decisions.reason: Speech quoted inside an oracle takes « », as the terms note sets it; the peoples' words end with "sus sendas", and the last two lines are the prophet's own (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "mafundisho" for *torah* at every level
decisions.reason: God's teaching going out to the nations is instruction for how to live (m1), not a law code; as at 1:10, Literal also says "mafundisho".

source.text: וְשָׁפַט֙ בֵּ֣ין הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְהוֹכִ֖יחַ לְעַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְכִתְּת֨וּ חַרְבוֹתָ֜ם לְאִתִּ֗ים וַחֲנִיתֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ לְמַזְמֵר֔וֹת לֹא־יִשָּׂ֨א ג֤וֹי אֶל־גּוֹי֙ חֶ֔רֶב וְלֹא־יִלְמְד֥וּ ע֖וֹד מִלְחָמָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he will judge between the nations and decide for peoples many, and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning knives. Not will lift up nation against nation sword, and not they will learn again war.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will judge between the nations and will decide for many peoples, \q and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning knives. \q Nation will not lift up sword against nation, \q and they will not learn war again.
en.B: He will be judge between the nations and settle the cases of many peoples. \q They will hammer their swords into plow blades and their spears into knives for pruning. \q No nation will raise the sword against another, \q and they will no longer learn how to wage war.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will settle arguments between nations and make fair decisions for many peoples. \q They will take their swords and hammer them into blades for plowing. They will turn their spears into knives for trimming vines. \q Nations will stop fighting one another. \q People will not even learn how to fight wars anymore.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} juzgará entre las naciones y decidirá por muchos pueblos, \q y forjarán sus espadas en rejas de arado y sus lanzas en podaderas. \q No alzará espada nación contra nación, \q y no aprenderán más la guerra.
es.B: Él será juez entre las naciones y resolverá los pleitos de muchos pueblos. \q Martillarán sus espadas hasta hacer de ellas hojas de arado, y de sus lanzas, cuchillos para podar. \q Ninguna nación levantará la espada contra otra, \q y ya no aprenderán a hacer la guerra.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} resolverá las disputas entre las naciones y tomará decisiones justas para muchos pueblos. \q Tomarán sus espadas y las martillarán hasta convertirlas en hojas para arar. Convertirán sus lanzas en cuchillos para podar las vides. \q Las naciones dejarán de pelear unas contra otras. \q La gente ni siquiera aprenderá a hacer la guerra.

sw.L: Naye atahukumu kati ya mataifa na kuamua mashauri ya watu wengi, \q nao watafua panga zao kuwa majembe na mikuki yao kuwa miundu. \q Taifa halitainua upanga juu ya taifa, \q wala hawatajifunza vita tena.
sw.B: Atakuwa mwamuzi kati ya mataifa na kuyamaliza mashauri ya watu wengi. \q Watazifua panga zao kuwa majembe, na mikuki yao kuwa visu vya kupogolea. \q Hakuna taifa litakaloinua upanga dhidi ya taifa jingine, \q wala hawatajifunza tena kupigana vita.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamaliza mabishano kati ya mataifa na kuwaamulia watu wengi kwa haki. \q Watachukua panga zao na kuzifua kuwa majembe ya kulimia. Watageuza mikuki yao kuwa visu vya kupogolea mizabibu. \q Mataifa yataacha kupigana. \q Watu hawatajifunza tena hata jinsi ya kupigana vita.

decisions.choice: judge ... decide: the LORD settles the nations' disputes
decisions.reason: The one who teaches in verse 3 is now judge between nations. The second verb means to decide what is right between two parties, to settle a case (Genesis 31:37; Job 9:33). Once he settles their quarrels, they no longer need weapons.

decisions.choice: plowshares ... pruning knives: tools for farming
decisions.reason: The first word is an iron farm blade, most likely the point of a plow, though it may be a hoe or digging tool (1 Samuel 13:20-21). The second is a knife for trimming vines (18:5). Weapons become tools for growing food.

decisions.choice: swords into plowshares: the same words as Micah 4:3, and turned around in Joel
decisions.reason: Micah 4:3 has the same lines. Joel 4:10 (3:10 in many Bibles) reverses them as a call to war: "Beat your plowshares into swords." "Learn war" means to train for it; even the skill of war will be forgotten.

decisions.choice: The LORD ... blades for plowing ... trimming vines
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one who judges, as in verse 3, and explains the two farm tools.

source.text: בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה בְּא֥וֹר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: House of Jacob, come and let us walk in [the] light of Yahweh.

en.L: House of Jacob, come, \q and let us walk in the light of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: House of Jacob, come! \q Let us walk by the light of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People of Israel, come! \q Let us live in the light {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives.

es.L: Casa de Jacob, {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, \q y andemos a la luz {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: ¡Casa de Jacob, {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}! \q Caminemos a la luz {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: ¡Pueblo de Israel, {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}! \q Vivamos en la luz que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos da.

sw.L: Nyumba ya Yakobo, njooni, \q na tutembee katika nuru ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Enyi nyumba ya Yakobo, njooni! \q Tutembee katika nuru ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Israeli, njooni! \q Tuishi katika nuru ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anatupa.

decisions.choice: come, let us walk: the nations' words of verse 3 turned to Israel
decisions.reason: The prophet takes up the call of the nations, "Come ... we will walk", and turns it on his own people. If the nations will one day come to learn the LORD's ways, the house of Jacob should walk in them now.

decisions.choice: the light of Yahweh: his guidance and his favor
decisions.reason: Light is what lets a person see the way, and so the guidance God gives (Psalm 119:105; Psalm 27:1). The book returns to this light when the nations come to it (60:1-3).

decisions.choice: People of Israel
decisions.reason: "House of Jacob" means the people descended from Jacob, whose other name was Israel. Literal and Balanced keep "house of Jacob".

source.text: כִּ֣י נָטַ֗שְׁתָּה עַמְּךָ֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּ֤י מָלְאוּ֙ מִקֶּ֔דֶם וְעֹֽנְנִ֖ים כַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּבְיַלְדֵ֥י נָכְרִ֖ים יַשְׂפִּֽיקוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For you have forsaken your people, [the] house of Jacob, for they are full from [the] east, and soothsayers like the Philistines, and with [the] children of foreigners they clap hands.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, the house of Jacob, \q for they are full from the east, and [are] soothsayers like the Philistines, \q and with the children of foreigners they clap hands.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have cast off {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, the house of Jacob, \q because they are crowded with what comes from the east and with soothsayers, as the Philistines are, \q and they strike hands with the sons of foreigners.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, the descendants of Jacob. \q They are full of customs from the lands to the east. They try to tell the future, as the Philistines do. \q They make deals with foreigners.

es.L: Porque has abandonado a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, la casa de Jacob, \q porque están llenos [de lo] del oriente, y [son] adivinos como los filisteos, \q y con los hijos de extranjeros chocan las manos.
es.B: Porque has desechado a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, la casa de Jacob, \q porque están repletos de lo que viene del oriente y de adivinos, como los filisteos, \q y cierran tratos con los hijos de extranjeros.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} te has alejado de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, los descendientes de Jacob. \q Están llenos de costumbres de los países del oriente. Tratan de adivinar el futuro, como hacen los filisteos. \q Hacen negocios con extranjeros.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umewaacha watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, nyumba ya Yakobo, \q kwa sababu wamejaa [mambo] ya mashariki, na [ni] wapiga ramli kama Wafilisti, \q na wanapeana mikono na wana wa wageni.
sw.B: Kwa maana umewatupa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, nyumba ya Yakobo, \q kwa sababu wamejaa mambo yatokayo mashariki na wapiga ramli kama walivyo Wafilisti, \q nao wanapeana mikono na wana wa wageni.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, umewaacha watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, wazao wa Yakobo. \q Wamejaa desturi za nchi za mashariki. Wanajaribu kutabiri mambo yajayo, kama Wafilisti wanavyofanya. \q Wanafanya mapatano na wageni.

decisions.choice: for you have forsaken: the prophet turns to speak to God
alternatives: Surely you have forsaken your people
decisions.reason: "You" is God, who has left his people to themselves. "For" gives the reason for the call of verse 5: the house of Jacob is not walking in the LORD's light, and he has given them up. The word may instead stress the statement ("Surely you have forsaken").

decisions.choice: full from the east, and soothsayers like the Philistines: full of foreign religious practices
alternatives: full of diviners from the east
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short: they are "full from the east", that is, full of what has come from the east, most likely ways of seeking hidden knowledge. Soothsayers read signs to tell the future, which the law of Moses forbids (Deuteronomy 18:10-14). The Philistines on the coast were known for it (2 Kings 1:2).

decisions.choice: they clap hands with the children of foreigners: they make agreements with foreigners
alternatives: they abound with the children of foreigners
decisions.reason: Striking hands seals a bargain or pledge (Proverbs 6:1; 17:18). Here it means they make deals and alliances with foreigners, and take on their ways with them. The verb may also mean that they abound with foreigners' children.

decisions.choice: cast off (Balanced); turned away from (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or abandon. Readable names the LORD as the one spoken to.

source.text: וַתִּמָּלֵ֤א אַרְצוֹ֙ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֖צֶה לְאֹצְרֹתָ֑יו וַתִּמָּלֵ֤א אַרְצוֹ֙ סוּסִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֖צֶה לְמַרְכְּבֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And has been filled its land [with] silver and gold, and no end to its treasures; and has been filled its land [with] horses, and no end to its chariots.

en.L: And its land is filled [with] silver and gold, \q and [there is] no end to its treasures; \q and its land is filled [with] horses, \q and [there is] no end to its chariots.
en.B: Silver and gold fill their land, \q and their treasures are beyond counting; \q horses fill their land, \q and their chariots are beyond counting.
en.R: Their country is packed with silver and gold, \q and their riches never run out. \q Their country is packed with war horses, \q and their chariots never run out.

es.L: Y su tierra está llena de plata y oro, \q y no [hay] fin para sus tesoros; \q y su tierra está llena de caballos, \q y no [hay] fin para sus carros.
es.B: La plata y el oro llenan su tierra, \q y sus tesoros no tienen número; \q los caballos llenan su tierra, \q y sus carros no tienen número.
es.R: Su país está repleto de plata y oro, \q y sus riquezas nunca se acaban. \q Su país está repleto de caballos de guerra, \q y sus carros nunca se acaban.

sw.L: Na nchi yake imejaa fedha na dhahabu, \q wala hazina zake hazina mwisho; \q na nchi yake imejaa farasi, \q wala magari yake ya vita hayana mwisho.
sw.B: Fedha na dhahabu zimeijaza nchi yao, \q na hazina zao hazihesabiki; \q farasi wameijaza nchi yao, \q na magari yao ya vita hayahesabiki.
sw.R: Nchi yao imejaa fedha na dhahabu tele, \q na mali zao hazimaliziki. \q Nchi yao imejaa farasi wa vita, \q na magari yao ya vita hayamaliziki.

decisions.choice: its land: the land of the house of Jacob
decisions.reason: In verses 7-8 the words for "its" and "his" are singular: the house of Jacob is spoken of as one. The meaning is their land, their treasures, their chariots.

decisions.choice: silver, gold, horses: the riches the king was told not to pile up
decisions.reason: The law for Israel's king forbade him to gather many horses or great amounts of silver and gold (Deuteronomy 17:16-17). Horses and chariots were the strength of an army, and the prophet warns against trusting in them rather than in God (31:1).

decisions.choice: war horses
decisions.reason: Readable says "war horses": the horses go with chariots and are a sign of military strength.

source.text: וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א אַרְצ֖וֹ אֱלִילִ֑ים לְמַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדָיו֙ יִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֔וּ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ אֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And has been filled its land [with] idols; to [the] work of its hands they bow down, to what have made its fingers.

en.L: And its land is filled [with] idols; \q to the work of its hands they bow down, to what its fingers have made.
en.B: Idols fill their land too. \q They worship things their own hands produced, objects shaped by their own fingers.
en.R: Their country is packed with worthless idols. \q They bow down and worship things they made themselves.

es.L: Y su tierra está llena de ídolos; \q ante la obra de sus manos se postran, ante lo que hicieron sus dedos.
es.B: También los ídolos llenan su tierra. \q Adoran cosas que fabricaron sus propias manos, objetos formados por sus propios dedos.
es.R: Su país está repleto de ídolos que no valen nada. \q Se inclinan y adoran cosas que ellos mismos hicieron.

sw.L: Na nchi yake imejaa sanamu; \q wanaisujudia kazi ya mikono yao, yale ambayo vidole vyao vimeyafanya.
sw.B: Sanamu nazo zimeijaza nchi yao. \q Wanaabudu vitu ambavyo mikono yao wenyewe ilivitengeneza, vitu vilivyoundwa kwa vidole vyao wenyewe.
sw.R: Nchi yao imejaa sanamu zisizo na thamani. \q Wanazisujudia na kuziabudu, nao ndio waliozitengeneza.

decisions.choice: idols: worthless gods, things that are nothing
decisions.reason: The word for idols sounds like the word for God but means something empty and worthless (Leviticus 19:4; Psalm 96:5). It is a key word of this chapter (verses 18 and 20).

decisions.choice: the work of their hands: worshiping what they made
decisions.reason: People bow down to objects they shaped themselves. Isaiah returns to this folly often (17:8; 44:9-20; compare Psalm 115:4-8).

decisions.choice: worthless idols
decisions.reason: Readable adds "worthless" to carry the sense of the word for idols.

source.text: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל־אִ֑ישׁ וְאַל־תִּשָּׂ֖א לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And is bowed down humankind, and is brought low each one; and do not lift up for them.

en.L: And humankind is bowed down, and each one is brought low; \q and do not forgive them.
en.B: So humankind sinks low, and each person is put down. \q Do not pardon them!
en.R: That is why people are being brought down, every one of them. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, do not forgive them!

es.L: Y el ser humano es humillado, y cada uno es abatido; \q y no los perdones.
es.B: Así la humanidad se rebaja, y cada persona es abatida. \q ¡No los perdones!
es.R: Por eso la gente está siendo humillada, todos ellos. \q ¡{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, no los perdones!

sw.L: Na mwanadamu ameinamishwa, na kila mtu ameshushwa; \q nawe usiwasamehe.
sw.B: Hivyo wanadamu wanashushwa chini, na kila mtu ananyenyekezwa. \q Usiwasamehe!
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu watu wanashushwa, kila mmoja wao. \q Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, usiwasamehe!

decisions.choice: humankind is bowed down: people are brought low because of their idols
alternatives: so people bow down, everyone stoops low (before idols)
decisions.reason: The two verbs follow from verse 8. People who bow to what they made are degraded by it, and God will humble them; verses 11 and 17 use the same two verbs for the day when he does. The verbs may also describe the people stooping before their idols.

decisions.choice: do not forgive them: the prophet asks God not to pardon
decisions.reason: The verb means "lift" or "carry"; with sins it means to take them away, to forgive (Exodus 34:7). Here the prophet asks God not to excuse such worship. The words could also mean "do not lift them up", which would echo the word "lifted up" through the chapter.

decisions.choice: the Masoretic text includes "do not forgive them"
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) does not have these words or verse 10. The Septuagint has them. The Masoretic text is followed here.

decisions.choice: LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one the prophet asks.

decisions.choice: SEÑOR addressed directly, with no "oh"
decisions.reason: YHWH addressed directly is "SEÑOR" with no "oh", as the terms note sets it from Psalm 19:15. Book-wide choice for chapters 1-20.

source.text: בּ֣וֹא בַצּ֔וּר וְהִטָּמֵ֖ן בֶּֽעָפָ֑ר מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר גְּאֹנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Go into the rock and hide yourself in the dust from before [the] dread of Yahweh and from [the] splendor of his majesty.

en.L: Go into the rock and hide yourself in the dust, \q from before the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from the splendor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majesty.
en.B: Get into the rocks! Bury yourself in the dust, \q away from the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majestic splendor!
en.R: Run into the caves in the rocks! Hide in holes in the ground! \q Hide from the fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brings and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great and shining majesty!

es.L: Entra en la roca y escóndete en el polvo, \q de delante del terror {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y del esplendor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestad.
es.B: ¡Métete entre las rocas! ¡Entiérrate en el polvo, \q lejos del terror {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestuoso esplendor!
es.R: ¡Corre a las cuevas de las rocas! ¡Escóndete en hoyos en la tierra! \q ¡Escóndete del miedo que trae {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestad grande y resplandeciente!

sw.L: Ingia mwambani, ujifiche mavumbini, \q mbele ya utisho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na mbele ya fahari ya enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Ingia katikati ya miamba! Jifiche mavumbini, \q mbali na utisho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na fahari ya enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}!
sw.R: Kimbilieni mapangoni mwa miamba! Jificheni katika mashimo ardhini! \q Jificheni mbali na hofu anayoleta {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuu inayong'aa!

decisions.choice: go in, hide: a command to each person
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular, spoken to each one. The command may be bitter irony, since no one can hide from God. Verses 19 and 21 tell of people doing just this.

decisions.choice: the dread of Yahweh, the splendor of his majesty: the terror and glory of his coming
decisions.reason: "Dread" is the terror his presence brings. "Splendor" and "majesty" describe his overwhelming greatness. These words return as a refrain in verses 19 and 21.

decisions.choice: the Masoretic text includes this verse
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) does not have this verse; see the note at verse 9. The Septuagint has it.

decisions.choice: caves in the rocks ... holes in the ground
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the rock" and "the dust" as places to hide, as verse 19 does.

source.text: עֵינֵ֞י גַּבְה֤וּת אָדָם֙ שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [The] eyes of [the] pride of humankind will be brought low, and will be bowed down [the] haughtiness of men, and will be exalted Yahweh alone in day the that.

en.L: The eyes of the pride of humankind will be brought low, \q and the haughtiness of people will be bowed down, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone will be exalted in that day.
en.B: The arrogant gaze of humankind will be lowered, \q people's lofty pride will be bent down, \q and on that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone will be lifted high.
en.R: Proud people will be made humble. \q People who think they are great will be brought down. \q On that day, only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be honored as great.

es.L: Los ojos del orgullo del ser humano serán abatidos, \q y la altivez de los hombres será humillada, \q y solo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} será exaltado en aquel día.
es.B: La mirada arrogante de la humanidad será abatida, \q el orgullo altivo de la gente será doblegado, \q y aquel día solo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} será enaltecido.
es.R: Los orgullosos serán humillados. \q Los que se creen grandes serán derribados. \q En ese día, solo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} será honrado como grande.

sw.L: Macho ya kiburi ya mwanadamu yatashushwa, \q na majivuno ya watu yatainamishwa, \q naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} peke yake atatukuzwa katika siku ile.
sw.B: Macho ya majivuno ya wanadamu yatashushwa, \q kiburi cha watu kitainamishwa, \q na siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} peke yake atainuliwa juu.
sw.R: Watu wenye kiburi watanyenyekezwa. \q Watu wanaojiona kuwa wakuu watashushwa. \q Wakati huo, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} peke yake ndiye atakayeheshimiwa kuwa mkuu.

decisions.choice: eyes of pride: the proud, haughty look
decisions.reason: Proud eyes look down on others (Proverbs 6:17; Psalm 18:28; Psalm 131:1).

decisions.choice: Yahweh alone will be exalted: only God will stand high
decisions.reason: The verb means to be set high, out of reach. All that people raise up will come down, and God alone will be seen as high. The line is repeated in verse 17.

decisions.choice: that day: the day of Yahweh
decisions.reason: "That day" is the day verse 12 announces, when God acts in judgment.

decisions.choice: honored as great
decisions.reason: Readable explains being "exalted": everyone will see that only the LORD is great.

decisions.choice: en aquel día (L); aquel día (B); en ese día / en ese tiempo (R)
decisions.reason: The formula "in that day" is set as the terms note gives it, as published from Joshua to Chronicles. Book-wide choice for chapters 1-20.

decisions.choice: "katika siku ile" (L), "siku hiyo" (B), "wakati huo" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *bayyom hahu* in the prophets (terms note); Readable's "wakati huo" also serves where the English Readable says "on that day". Recorded once for this block.

source.text: כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת עַ֥ל כָּל־גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם וְעַ֖ל כָּל־נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: For a day [belongs] to Yahweh of hosts against every proud and lofty [thing], and against every lifted up [thing], and [it will be] low,

en.L: For [there is] a day for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts against everything proud and lofty, \q and against everything lifted up, and [it will be] brought low,
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has set a day against everything proud and towering, \q against everything raised high, and it will be brought down,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has chosen a day when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will act against everything that is proud and high. \q He will bring all of it down.

es.L: Porque [hay] un día para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos contra todo lo soberbio y altivo, \q y contra todo lo enaltecido, y [será] abatido,
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos ha fijado un día contra todo lo soberbio y elevado, \q contra todo lo que se alza en alto, y será derribado,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos ha escogido un día en que actuará contra todo lo que es orgulloso y alto. \q Lo derribará todo.

sw.L: Kwa maana [kuna] siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi juu ya kila kilicho na kiburi na kilicho juu, \q na juu ya kila kilichoinuliwa, nacho [kitashushwa],
sw.B: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ameweka siku dhidi ya kila kitu chenye kiburi na kirefu, \q dhidi ya kila kitu kilichoinuliwa juu, nacho kitashushwa,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amechagua siku atakapopambana na kila kitu chenye kiburi na kilicho juu. \q Atakishusha chote.

decisions.choice: a day for Yahweh of hosts: the day of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of a day that belongs to the LORD, when he acts in judgment and shows who he is (Amos 5:18-20; Zephaniah 1:14-18; Isaiah 13:6-9). In verses 12-16 everything that stands high is listed under it.

decisions.choice: lifted up: the word used of Zion's mountain in verse 2
decisions.reason: Verse 2 said the mountain of the LORD's house will be "lifted up" above the hills. Here the same word marks every proud height that will come down. Only his mountain will stay high.

decisions.choice: has chosen a day when he will act
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "a day for the LORD" as a day he has set to act.

source.text: וְעַל֙ כָּל־אַרְזֵ֣י הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־אַלּוֹנֵ֥י הַבָּשָֽׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: and against all [the] cedars of the Lebanon, the lofty and the lifted up, and against all [the] oaks of the Bashan,

en.L: and against all the cedars of Lebanon, the lofty and the lifted up, \q and against all the oaks of Bashan,
en.B: against all the cedars of Lebanon, high and towering, \q and against all the oaks of Bashan,
en.R: He will act against the tall cedar trees of Lebanon \q and the mighty oak trees of Bashan.

es.L: y contra todos los cedros del Líbano, altos y enaltecidos, \q y contra todas las encinas de Basán,
es.B: contra todos los cedros del Líbano, altos y elevados, \q y contra todas las encinas de Basán,
es.R: Actuará contra los altos cedros del Líbano \q y contra las robustas encinas de Basán.

sw.L: na juu ya mierezi yote ya Lebanoni, iliyo mirefu na iliyoinuliwa, \q na juu ya mialoni yote ya Bashani,
sw.B: dhidi ya mierezi yote ya Lebanoni, mirefu na iliyoinuka juu, \q na dhidi ya mialoni yote ya Bashani,
sw.R: Atapambana na miti mirefu ya mierezi ya Lebanoni \q na miti mikubwa ya mialoni ya Bashani.

decisions.choice: cedars of Lebanon, oaks of Bashan: the tallest and strongest trees known
decisions.reason: The cedars of Lebanon, in the mountains north of Israel, were the finest timber of the region; Bashan, east of the Jordan, was known for its oaks. Tyre made ship masts of the one and oars of the other (Ezekiel 27:5-6).

decisions.choice: lofty and lifted up: great trees as a picture of human pride
decisions.reason: The prophets use tall trees for proud kings and nations (10:33-34; Ezekiel 31:3-10; Zechariah 11:1-2). Here the trees may stand for proud people as well as for the trees themselves.

decisions.choice: He will act against
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the verb of verse 12 so that each line stands as a sentence.

source.text: וְעַ֖ל כָּל־הֶהָרִ֣ים הָרָמִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־הַגְּבָע֥וֹת הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: and against all the mountains the lofty, and against all the hills the lifted up,

en.L: and against all the lofty mountains, \q and against all the hills that are lifted up,
en.B: against all the towering mountains, \q against all the hills raised high,
en.R: He will act against all the high mountains \q and tall hills.

es.L: y contra todos los montes altos, \q y contra todas las colinas enaltecidas,
es.B: contra todos los montes elevados, \q contra todas las colinas que se alzan en alto,
es.R: Actuará contra todos los montes altos \q y las colinas elevadas.

sw.L: na juu ya milima yote mirefu, \q na juu ya vilima vyote vilivyoinuliwa,
sw.B: dhidi ya milima yote mirefu, \q dhidi ya vilima vyote vilivyoinuka juu,
sw.R: Atapambana na milima yote mirefu \q na vilima virefu.

decisions.choice: the mountains and hills: every height except the LORD's own mountain
decisions.reason: In verse 2 the mountain of the LORD's house is raised above the mountains and the hills. Here every other mountain and hill is brought low (compare 40:4).

decisions.choice: He will act against
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

source.text: וְעַ֖ל כָּל־מִגְדָּ֣ל גָּבֹ֑הַוְעַ֖ל כָּל־חוֹמָ֥ה בְצוּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and against every tower high, and against every wall fortified,

en.L: and against every high tower, \q and against every fortified wall,
en.B: against every tall tower, \q against every wall built strong,
en.R: He will act against every tall tower \q and every strong wall built for defense.

es.L: y contra toda torre alta, \q y contra todo muro fortificado,
es.B: contra toda torre elevada, \q contra todo muro bien fortificado,
es.R: Actuará contra toda torre alta \q y contra todo muro fuerte construido para la defensa.

sw.L: na juu ya kila mnara mrefu, \q na juu ya kila ukuta wenye ngome,
sw.B: dhidi ya kila mnara mrefu, \q dhidi ya kila ukuta uliojengwa imara,
sw.R: Atapambana na kila mnara mrefu \q na kila ukuta imara uliojengwa kwa ajili ya ulinzi.

decisions.choice: high tower, fortified wall: the defenses of a city
decisions.reason: Towers and walls protected cities against attack. Kings of Judah in Isaiah's time built them (2 Chronicles 26:9; 27:3-4). The prophet warns against trusting them rather than God (22:8-11).

decisions.choice: He will act against ... built for defense
decisions.reason: As in verse 13; Readable explains "fortified".

source.text: וְעַ֖ל כָּל־אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־שְׂכִיּ֥וֹת הַחֶמְדָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and against all [the] ships of Tarshish, and against all the vessels of the desire.

en.L: and against all the ships of Tarshish, \q and against all the vessels of delight.
en.B: against all the ships of Tarshish, \q and against every splendid vessel.
en.R: He will act against the great trading ships \q and against every beautiful boat.

es.L: y contra todas las naves de Tarsis, \q y contra todas las embarcaciones de deleite.
es.B: contra todas las naves de Tarsis, \q y contra toda embarcación espléndida.
es.R: Actuará contra los grandes barcos mercantes \q y contra toda embarcación hermosa.

sw.L: na juu ya merikebu zote za Tarshishi, \q na juu ya vyombo vyote vya kupendeza.
sw.B: dhidi ya merikebu zote za Tarshishi, \q na dhidi ya kila chombo cha fahari.
sw.R: Atapambana na meli kubwa za biashara \q na kila mashua nzuri.

decisions.choice: ships of Tarshish: large ships for trade by sea
decisions.reason: Tarshish was a distant port far to the west (Jonah 1:3). "Ships of Tarshish" were the big ships that carried trade over long distances (1 Kings 10:22; Isaiah 23:1), and the name came to be used for any such ship.

decisions.choice: vessels of delight: fine ships, objects of admiration
decisions.reason: The first word is rare and its sense uncertain. Set beside the ships of Tarshish it most likely means ships or craft; it may instead mean any fine carved work or display. The Septuagint reads something like "every sight of beautiful ships".

decisions.choice: great trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ships of Tarshish" and adds the verb as in verse 13.

decisions.choice: naves de Tarsis (L, B); grandes barcos mercantes (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets it from 1 Kings 10:22 and 22:49: L and B keep the name, R says what these ships were, as the English R does. Book-wide choice for chapters 1-20.

decisions.choice: "merikebu za Tarshishi" (L, B), "meli kubwa za biashara" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording (Psalm 48:8); Readable says what the ships were, as the English Readable does (m1).

source.text: וְשַׁח֙ גַּבְה֣וּת הָאָדָ֔ם וְשָׁפֵ֖ל ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be bowed down [the] pride of humankind, and will be brought low [the] haughtiness of men, and will be exalted Yahweh alone in day the that.

en.L: And the pride of humankind will be bowed down, \q and the haughtiness of people will be brought low, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone will be exalted in that day.
en.B: Humankind's pride will be bent down, \q people's lofty airs laid low, \q and on that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone will be lifted high.
en.R: Proud people will be brought down. \q People who think they are great will be made humble. \q On that day, only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be honored as great.

es.L: Y el orgullo del ser humano será humillado, \q y la altivez de los hombres será abatida, \q y solo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} será exaltado en aquel día.
es.B: El orgullo de la humanidad será doblegado, \q los aires de grandeza de la gente serán abatidos, \q y aquel día solo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} será enaltecido.
es.R: Los orgullosos serán derribados. \q Los que se creen grandes serán humillados. \q En ese día, solo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} será honrado como grande.

sw.L: Na kiburi cha mwanadamu kitainamishwa, \q na majivuno ya watu yatashushwa, \q naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} peke yake atatukuzwa katika siku ile.
sw.B: Kiburi cha wanadamu kitainamishwa, \q majivuno ya watu yatashushwa chini, \q na siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} peke yake atainuliwa juu.
sw.R: Watu wenye kiburi watashushwa. \q Watu wanaojiona kuwa wakuu watanyenyekezwa. \q Wakati huo, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} peke yake ndiye atakayeheshimiwa kuwa mkuu.

decisions.choice: the refrain of verse 11, with the verbs exchanged
decisions.reason: Verse 11 is repeated with its two verbs swapped, to close the list of verses 12-16. Everything in that list is summed up as human pride.

decisions.choice: Yahweh alone will be exalted
decisions.reason: See the note at verse 11.

decisions.choice: honored as great
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

source.text: וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And the idols entirely will pass away.

en.L: And the idols will entirely pass away.
en.B: As for the idols, they will be gone, every one.
en.R: The idols will all be gone for good.

es.L: Y los ídolos pasarán por completo.
es.B: En cuanto a los ídolos, desaparecerán todos.
es.R: Los ídolos desaparecerán todos para siempre.

sw.L: Na sanamu zitapita kabisa.
sw.B: Na sanamu zitatoweka, kila moja.
sw.R: Sanamu zote zitatoweka kabisa.

decisions.choice: the idols will entirely pass away: all of them, completely
decisions.reason: The verb is singular with a plural subject: the idols vanish as one whole. The word "entirely" means complete, whole. The verse stands alone as a short line between the two refrains, and verse 20 tells how it happens.

source.text: וּבָ֨אוּ֙ בִּמְעָר֣וֹת צֻרִ֔ים וּבִמְחִלּ֖וֹת עָפָ֑ר מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will go into caves of rocks and into holes of dust, from before [the] dread of Yahweh and from [the] splendor of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.

en.L: And they will go into caves of rocks and into holes of the dust, \q from before the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from the splendor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majesty, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rises to terrify the earth.
en.B: People will crawl into caves in the rock and pits in the ground, \q away from the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majestic splendor, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rises up to make the earth shudder.
en.R: People will run into caves in the rocks and holes in the ground. \q They will hide from the fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brings and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great and shining majesty. \q They will hide when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stands up to shake the earth.

es.L: Y entrarán en las cuevas de las rocas y en los hoyos del polvo, \q de delante del terror {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y del esplendor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestad, \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se levante para aterrar la tierra.
es.B: La gente se meterá en las cuevas de la roca y en los pozos de la tierra, \q lejos del terror {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestuoso esplendor, \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se levante para hacer estremecer la tierra.
es.R: La gente correrá a las cuevas de las rocas y a los hoyos en la tierra. \q Se esconderán del miedo que trae {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestad grande y resplandeciente. \q Se esconderán cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se levante para sacudir la tierra.

sw.L: Nao wataingia katika mapango ya miamba na katika mashimo ya mavumbi, \q mbele ya utisho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na mbele ya fahari ya enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q atakaposimama aitetemeshe dunia.
sw.B: Watu watatambaa kuingia mapangoni mwa miamba na mashimoni ardhini, \q mbali na utisho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na fahari ya enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q atakaposimama kuitikisa dunia kwa hofu.
sw.R: Watu watakimbilia mapangoni mwa miamba na mashimoni ardhini. \q Watajificha mbali na hofu anayoleta {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuu inayong'aa. \q Watajificha atakaposimama kuitikisa dunia.

decisions.choice: caves of the rocks: the command of verse 10 now carried out
decisions.reason: What verse 10 commanded, people now do. Hosea 10:8 has people beg the mountains to cover them, and Revelation 6:15-16 takes up these words for the day of God's wrath.

decisions.choice: when he rises: when God stands up to act
decisions.reason: God "rises" as a judge or warrior getting up to act (Psalm 76:10; Isaiah 33:10).

decisions.choice: to terrify the earth: to make the whole earth shake with dread
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike with terror or awe. In the Hebrew it sounds like the word for "the earth" that follows, a play on sound that makes the line ring.

decisions.choice: make the earth shudder (Balanced); shake the earth (Readable)
decisions.reason: The terror shows itself as trembling; Literal keeps "terrify".

source.text: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ יַשְׁלִ֣יךְ הָאָדָ֔ם אֵ֚ת אֱלִילֵ֣י כַסְפּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֖ת אֱלִילֵ֣י זְהָב֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָֽשׂוּ־לוֹ֙ לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֔ת לַחְפֹּ֥ר פֵּר֖וֹת וְלָעֲטַלֵּפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: In day the that will throw away humankind the idols of its silver and the idols of its gold which they made for it to bow down, to the digging of rats and to the bats,

en.L: In that day humankind will throw away its idols of silver and its idols of gold, \q which they made for it to bow down [to], \q to the moles and to the bats,
en.B: On that day people will fling away their idols of silver and their idols of gold, \q made for them to bow down to, \q out to the moles and the bats,
en.R: On that day, people will throw away the silver and gold idols they made to worship. \q They will toss them to the moles and the bats.

es.L: En aquel día el ser humano arrojará sus ídolos de plata y sus ídolos de oro, \q que le hicieron para postrarse [ante ellos], \q a los topos y a los murciélagos,
es.B: Aquel día la gente tirará sus ídolos de plata y sus ídolos de oro, \q hechos para que se postraran ante ellos, \q a los topos y a los murciélagos,
es.R: En ese día, la gente tirará los ídolos de plata y oro que hicieron para adorarlos. \q Se los arrojarán a los topos y a los murciélagos.

sw.L: Katika siku ile mwanadamu atazitupa sanamu zake za fedha na sanamu zake za dhahabu, \q walizomfanyia ili azisujudie, \q kwa fuko na kwa popo,
sw.B: Siku hiyo watu watazitupilia mbali sanamu zao za fedha na sanamu zao za dhahabu, \q walizotengenezewa ili wazisujudie, \q wazitupe kwa fuko na kwa popo,
sw.R: Wakati huo watu watazitupa sanamu za fedha na dhahabu walizotengeneza ili kuziabudu. \q Watazitupia fuko na popo.

decisions.choice: they will throw away their idols: the idols pass away (verse 18)
decisions.reason: Verse 18 said the idols would vanish; here people themselves throw them away. Isaiah says the same in 30:22 and 31:7.

decisions.choice: moles and bats: creatures of dark, unclean places
decisions.reason: Bats were unclean animals (Leviticus 11:19), living in caves and ruins. The first creature is uncertain: the Masoretic text divides it into two words, "to dig" and a word like "rats"; read as one word it most likely names moles or shrews. Either way the idols are thrown where only such animals live.

decisions.choice: out to the moles and the bats
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew order, where the moles and bats come last, so that the sentence runs on into verse 21.

source.text: לָבוֹא֙ בְּנִקְר֣וֹת הַצֻּרִ֔ים וּבִסְעִפֵ֖י הַסְּלָעִ֑ים מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: to go into [the] clefts of the rocks and into [the] crevices of the cliffs, from before [the] dread of Yahweh and from [the] splendor of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.

en.L: to go into the clefts of the rocks and into the crevices of the cliffs, \q from before the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from the splendor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majesty, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rises to terrify the earth.
en.B: so that they can creep into the cracks of the rocks and the crevices of the crags, \q away from the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majestic splendor, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rises up to make the earth shudder.
en.R: Then they will run into cracks in the rocks and gaps in the cliffs. \q They will hide from the fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brings and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great and shining majesty, \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stands up to shake the earth.

es.L: para entrar en las hendiduras de las rocas y en las grietas de los peñascos, \q de delante del terror {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y del esplendor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestad, \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se levante para aterrar la tierra.
es.B: para poder meterse en las hendiduras de las rocas y en las grietas de los peñascos, \q lejos del terror {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestuoso esplendor, \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se levante para hacer estremecer la tierra.
es.R: Entonces correrán a las grietas de las rocas y a las hendiduras de los acantilados. \q Se esconderán del miedo que trae {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} majestad grande y resplandeciente, \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se levante para sacudir la tierra.

sw.L: ili waingie katika nyufa za miamba na katika mapango ya majabali, \q mbele ya utisho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na mbele ya fahari ya enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q atakaposimama aitetemeshe dunia.
sw.B: ili waweze kutambaa kuingia katika nyufa za miamba na mapango ya majabali, \q mbali na utisho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na fahari ya enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q atakaposimama kuitikisa dunia kwa hofu.
sw.R: Kisha watakimbilia katika nyufa za miamba na mapango ya majabali. \q Watajificha mbali na hofu anayoleta {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na enzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuu inayong'aa, \q atakaposimama kuitikisa dunia.

decisions.choice: to go in: why they throw the idols away
decisions.reason: The verse continues verse 20. People drop their idols so that they can flee into the rocks with free hands.

decisions.choice: the clefts of the rocks: the place where Moses was hidden
decisions.reason: The same phrase in the singular is used when God put Moses in "the cleft of the rock" so that he could see God's glory pass by (Exodus 33:22). Here people hide in the clefts to escape his splendor.

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and links it to verse 20 with "then".

source.text: חִדְל֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מִן־הָ֣אָדָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְשָׁמָ֖ה בְּאַפּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־בַמֶּ֥ה נֶחְשָׁ֖ב הֽוּא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Cease for yourselves from humankind who breath [is] in his nostril, for at what is he accounted?

en.L: Cease for yourselves from humankind, who [has] breath in his nostrils, \q for at what is he to be accounted?
en.B: Have done with humankind, who live by a breath in the nostrils, \q for what are they worth?
en.R: Stop trusting in human beings. Their life is only a breath that can stop at any time. \q Why should you think they are important?

es.L: {{plural_you:Apártense|Apartaos}} del ser humano, que [tiene] aliento en su nariz, \q porque ¿en qué ha de ser estimado?
es.B: {{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} de apoyarse en el ser humano, que vive de un soplo en la nariz, \q porque ¿qué valor tiene?
es.R: {{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} de confiar en los seres humanos. Su vida es solo un soplo que puede acabarse en cualquier momento. \q ¿Por qué {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que son importantes?

sw.L: Jiepusheni na mwanadamu, ambaye pumzi [yake iko] puani mwake, \q kwa maana yeye ahesabiwa kuwa kitu gani?
sw.B: Achaneni na mwanadamu, ambaye uhai wake ni pumzi tu puani, \q kwa maana ana thamani gani?
sw.R: Acheni kuwategemea wanadamu. Uhai wao ni pumzi tu, inayoweza kukoma wakati wowote. \q Kwa nini mnawaona kuwa watu muhimu?

decisions.choice: cease from humankind: stop relying on people
decisions.reason: The command is plural, spoken to the hearers. To "cease from" someone is to stop leaning on him, to have done with him. The question at the end means that a mortal counts for nothing next to God.

decisions.choice: breath in his nostrils: a mortal whose life is only a breath
decisions.reason: God breathed into the first man's nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). Human life lasts as long as that breath (Psalm 146:3-4; Job 27:3).

decisions.choice: the Masoretic text includes this verse
decisions.reason: The Septuagint does not have verse 22. The Masoretic text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Have done with ... what are they worth (Balanced); Stop trusting ... Why should you think they are important (Readable)
decisions.reason: The singular "he" and "his" refer to humankind as a whole, so Balanced and Readable use "they".
